section_title: ALS, Frontotemporal Dementia, and Other Neurodegenerative Conditions
thesis: In ALS, FTD, prion disease, multiple sclerosis and traumatic encephalopathy the inhibitory phenotype is real and well measured at the level of cortical physiology, but it is almost entirely a parvalbumin and bulk-GABA story: direct quantification of SST interneurons in human ALS or FTLD cortex was not retrieved, and the influential account in which hyperactive SST cells disinhibit layer 5 by suppressing PV cells rests on a single mouse TDP-43 study that has not been independently replicated in ten years.
scope_notes: ALS, FTD and other conditions; keep scope to SST/interneuron-relevant evidence.

findings.claim: Progressive impairment of dynein function does not cause loss of any major spinal interneuron population, including GABAergic and parvalbumin-positive cells, despite motor axonal pathology — a negative result bounding the generality of interneuron vulnerability in motor neuron disease models.
findings.claim_source_sentence: Contrary to our original hypothesis, we observed no significant loss of any major interneuron population, including cholinergic, GABAergic, parvalbumin- and calbindin-positive cells, across genotypes with progressively reduced dynein activity.
findings.evidence: Quantification of cholinergic, GABAergic, parvalbumin- and calbindin-positive interneuron populations across dynein-mutant genotypes.
findings.effect_size: No significant loss of any major interneuron population across genotypes (null result)
findings.effect_size_source_sentence: Contrary to our original hypothesis, we observed no significant loss of any major interneuron population, including cholinergic, GABAergic, parvalbumin- and calbindin-positive cells, across genotypes with progressively reduced dynein activity.

findings.claim: The C9orf72 promoter is active in inhibitory interneurons as well as excitatory neurons throughout brain and spinal cord, providing a cell-autonomous route by which C9orf72 mutations could affect interneuron function.

findings.evidence: Reporter-based mapping of C9orf72 promoter activity across neuronal classes in mouse brain and spinal cord.
findings.study_system: C9orf72 promoter reporter mouse, brain and spinal cord (histology)

findings.claim: In behavioural-variant frontotemporal dementia and progressive supranuclear palsy, generative modelling of cortical network physiology indicates increased tonic inhibition of deep inhibitory interneuron populations, interpreted as reduced activity of that population.
findings.claim_source_sentence: The increased tonic inhibition of these interneurons identified in our patients is considered to decrease the activity of this population, and this may be indicative of an overriding loss of deep inhibitory population activity in patients, either due to synaptic or neurotransmitter deficits.
findings.evidence: Magnetoencephalography with dynamic causal modelling of cortical microcircuits combined with a GABA-reuptake inhibitor (tiagabine) challenge and magnetic resonance spectroscopy GABA measurement in patients.
findings.effect_size: Interaction between tiagabine versus placebo and GABA concentration at inhibitory synapses on deep cortico-cortical projection neurons

findings.study_system: Human patients with bvFTD and PSP (MEG, DCM, pharmacological challenge)

findings.claim: Long-interval intracortical inhibition, a GABA-B-receptor-mediated measure, is not different between people with and without ALS and does not track disease progression, contrasting with the robust reduction of GABA-A-mediated short-interval inhibition.
findings.claim_source_sentence: Conclusion In summary, our work demonstrates that LICI is similar in people with and without ALS and does not relate to measures of disease progression or stage.
findings.evidence: Threshold-tracking paired-pulse TMS measurement of long-interval intracortical inhibition at multiple interstimulus intervals in ALS patients and healthy controls.
findings.effect_size: No significant difference in LICIPA measures between ALS and controls (P = 0.06–0.52)
findings.effect_size_source_sentence: For LICIPA measures, we also found no significant differences between healthy controls and those individuals with spinal-onset ALS where LICI was recorded in the hand on the side of symptom onset (P = 0.06–0.52), with the only trend (P = 0.06) observed being modestly higher LICIPA-100 ms i
findings.study_system: Human ALS patients and healthy controls, paired-pulse TMS

findings.claim: Meta-analysis of threshold-tracking TMS studies shows a large, consistent reduction of short-interval intracortical inhibition in ALS, making GABAergic inhibitory interneuron dysfunction the most robust cortical excitability signature of the disease.
findings.claim_source_sentence: A significant reduction of mean SICI was reported in ALS patients with evidence of moderate heterogeneity (SMD −0.99, 95% CI −1.12 to −0.87, p < 0.001; Q = 38.61, p < 0.05; I 2 = 40%; Figure 2).
findings.evidence: Systematic review and meta-analysis of paired-pulse threshold-tracking TMS studies comparing SICI and other excitability parameters in ALS patients versus controls.
findings.effect_size_source_sentence: A significant reduction of mean SICI was reported in ALS patients with evidence of moderate heterogeneity (SMD −0.99, 95% CI −1.12 to −0.87, p < 0.001; Q = 38.61, p < 0.05; I 2 = 40%; Figure 2).
findings.study_system: Human ALS patients across pooled TMS studies (meta-analysis)

findings.claim: Transcriptomic profiling of ALS brainstem identifies downregulation of the interneuron neuropeptides somatostatin, NPY and CCK among the transcripts linked to bulbar symptom development, extending SST-interneuron involvement in ALS beyond motor cortex.
findings.claim_source_sentence: Of particular interest were five downregulated transcripts in the brainstem, which could be functionally linked to the development of BSP, i.e., CHGA, C1QL2, SST, NPY, and CCK.
findings.evidence: RNA sequencing with digital droplet PCR validation and immunohistochemistry in post-mortem ALS brainstem tissue versus controls.
findings.effect_size: SST among five transcripts significantly downregulated in ALS brainstem (validated by ddPCR)
findings.study_system: Human post-mortem ALS brainstem tissue, transcriptomics and immunohistochemistry

findings.claim: In Creutzfeldt-Jakob disease the perineuronal extracellular matrix surrounding parvalbumin GABAergic interneurons is destroyed early, before and possibly causing the loss of these interneurons.
findings.claim_source_sentence: GABA-interneurons immunoreactive (IR) for the calcium-binding protein parvalbumin are lost during the early stages of Creutzfeldt-Jakob disease (CJD) and diminution in their number may partially account for the neurological disturbances manifested in patients suffering from this condition.
findings.evidence: Histochemical analysis of perineuronal nets and parvalbumin immunoreactivity in post-mortem CJD brain.
findings.effect_size: Qualitative: early destruction of perineuronal nets around parvalbumin interneurons; no numeric effect size reported in abstract
findings.study_system: Human Creutzfeldt-Jakob disease post-mortem brain tissue

findings.claim: Across human prion disease and rodent scrapie models, parvalbumin-positive GABAergic neuronal subpopulations and their extracellular matrix are selectively altered, making calcium-binding-protein immunohistochemistry a marker of inhibitory pathology in prion disease.
findings.claim_source_sentence: The study of calcium-binding proteins revealed an alteration of the parvalbumin positive GABAergic neuronal subpopulation.
findings.evidence: Comparative immunohistochemistry for parvalbumin and calbindin D-28K with extracellular matrix staining in human prion disease and rodent scrapie.
findings.effect_size: Qualitative alteration of the parvalbumin-positive GABAergic subpopulation; no numeric effect size in abstract
findings.study_system: Human prion disease brain tissue and rodent scrapie models

findings.claim: In ME7 prion-infected mice the perineuronal net around hippocampal parvalbumin interneurons is progressively lost in parallel with microglial activation, yet the parvalbumin interneurons themselves survive, dissociating matrix degradation from interneuron death.
findings.claim_source_sentence: No significant loss of PV-positive interneurons was observed.
findings.evidence: Time-course immunohistochemistry of microglial activation, PrP accumulation, PV interneuron counts and Wisteria floribunda agglutinin staining in ventral CA1 and subiculum at 4–20 weeks post-inoculation.
findings.effect_size: Perineuronal net loss without significant change in PV interneuron number across 4–20 weeks post-injection
findings.study_system: ME7 prion-infected mouse hippocampus (ventral CA1 and subiculum)

findings.claim: Midbrain dopamine depletion alone is sufficient to break down perineuronal nets, reduce GABAergic inhibition, produce network hyperexcitability and cause progressive parvalbumin interneuron loss, showing that interneuron vulnerability in neurodegeneration can arise without amyloid, tau or alpha-synuclein pathology.
findings.claim_source_sentence: They also demonstrate that DA depletion is sufficient to trigger PNN breakdown, reduce GABAergic inhibition, network hyperexcitability, and cause progressive PV-IN loss independently of canonical protein aggregates like Aβ, tau or α-synuclein, characteristic of AD, DLB or AD-PD.
findings.evidence: Mouse midbrain dopamine lesion with hippocampal electrophysiology, perineuronal net and PV interneuron quantification, and D2/D3 agonist rescue.
findings.effect_size: Quinpirole restored perineuronal net integrity and increased inhibitory postsynaptic event frequency (direction reported; no numeric value in abstract)
findings.study_system: Mouse model of midbrain dopamine depletion, hippocampal PV interneurons

findings.claim: Seventy-two hours after unilateral traumatic brain injury, contralateral somatostatin interneurons switch L-type calcium channel alpha subunits from CaV1.2 to CaV1.3, become more excitable, and this adaptation coincides with recovery from early network hyperactivity — an compensatory rather than degenerative SST interneuron response.
findings.claim_source_sentence: This switch was associated with 1) increased excitability of single SST interneurons in patch-clamp recordings and (2) a recovery from early network hyperactivity in the contralateral hemisphere in microelectrode array recordings of acute slices.
findings.evidence: FACS isolation and mass spectrometry of GAD67-GFP interneurons plus patch-clamp and multielectrode array recordings in the contralateral cortex after unilateral TBI in juvenile mice.
findings.effect_size: Switch of two L-type VGCC alpha subunits (CaV1.3 increased, CaV1.2 ablated); electrophysiological effects blocked by 100 nM isradipine
findings.effect_size_source_sentence: The electrophysiological changes were sensitive to pharmacological blockade of CaV1.3 (isradipine, 100 nM).
findings.study_system: GAD67-GFP knock-in mice, contralateral cortex 72 h after unilateral traumatic brain injury

findings.claim: Controlled cortical impact injury selectively depletes parvalbumin immunoreactive interneurons in the peri-injury cortex by 71% while leaving somatostatin interneuron and excitatory neuron numbers intact, demonstrating subtype-selective interneuron vulnerability to trauma.
findings.claim_source_sentence: Although CCI failed to alter the number of excitatory neurons or somatostatin-expressing interneurons in the peri-injury zone, it significantly decreased the density of parvalbumin (PV) immunoreactive cells by 71%.
findings.evidence: Immunohistochemical cell counts and slice electrophysiology of interneuron subtypes in the peri-injury cortex of mice after controlled cortical impact.
findings.effect_size: 71% decrease in parvalbumin immunoreactive cell density; no change in somatostatin interneuron number
findings.effect_size_source_sentence: Although CCI failed to alter the number of excitatory neurons or somatostatin-expressing interneurons in the peri-injury zone, it significantly decreased the density of parvalbumin (PV) immunoreactive cells by 71%.
findings.study_system: Mouse peri-injury neocortex after controlled cortical impact traumatic brain injury

findings.claim: Enhancing glutamate uptake with ceftriaxone after fluid percussion injury preserves intracortical inhibition and parvalbumin interneuron function in rat motor cortex, supporting excitotoxic damage to PV interneurons as the mechanism of post-traumatic disinhibition.
findings.claim_source_sentence: The ensuing glutamate excitotoxicity disproportionately damages vulnerable GABAergic parvalbumin-positive inhibitory interneurons, resulting in a progressively worsening cortical excitatory:inhibitory imbalance due to a loss of GABAergic inhibitory tone, as evidenced by chronic post-trauma
findings.evidence: Rat fluid percussion injury with long-interval paired-pulse TMS-mechanomyography, quantitative PCR and immunohistochemistry after ceftriaxone treatment.
findings.effect_size: Qualitative: ceftriaxone preserved intracortical inhibition and PV interneuron measures; no numeric effect size in abstract
findings.study_system: Rat motor cortex after lateral fluid percussion traumatic brain injury

findings.claim: After repetitive mild TBI the excitation-inhibition imbalance evolves: early glutamate elevation gives way at six weeks to depressed GABA, reduced per-cell parvalbumin expression and reduced gamma EEG power, with increased seizure susceptibility.
findings.claim_source_sentence: However, whereas increased Glu dominated the E/I 1 week after rmTBI, Glu concentration normalized and the E/I was instead characterized by depressed GABA, reduced per-PVI parvalbumin expression, and reduced gamma EEG power at the 6-week post-rmTBI time point.
findings.evidence: Longitudinal MRS, EEG, perineuronal net and parvalbumin immunohistochemistry and seizure threshold testing after repetitive mild TBI in rodents.
findings.effect_size: Timeline: glutamate elevation at 1 week versus GABA depression, reduced per-PVI parvalbumin and reduced gamma power at 6 weeks
findings.effect_size_source_sentence: However, whereas increased Glu dominated the E/I 1 week after rmTBI, Glu concentration normalized and the E/I was instead characterized by depressed GABA, reduced per-PVI parvalbumin expression, and reduced gamma EEG power at the 6-week post-rmTBI time point.
findings.study_system: Rodent model of repetitive mild traumatic brain injury (concussion), cortex

findings.claim: Hilar somatostatin interneurons that survive pilocarpine status epilepticus receive increased excitatory synaptic input and show anatomical changes that would raise their inhibitory output, a compensatory response of the surviving SST population to partial interneuron loss.
findings.claim_source_sentence: In sum, these changes would be expected to increase the inhibitory output of surviving SOM interneurons and in part compensate for interneuronal loss in the epileptogenic hippocampus.
findings.evidence: Whole-cell recordings and anatomical reconstruction of GFP-labelled hilar somatostatin interneurons in the pilocarpine mouse model of temporal lobe epilepsy.
findings.effect_size: Increased excitatory input onto surviving SOM interneurons (direction reported; no numeric value in abstract)
findings.study_system: Mouse dentate gyrus hilus after pilocarpine status epilepticus (GIN GFP somatostatin interneurons)

findings.claim: The spiny somatostatinergic hilar interneurons that are selectively lost in epilepsy target granule cell dendritic spines, with 67% of their inhibitory synapses placed on spines that also receive an excitatory contact, placing SST interneuron output at the site of excitatory input control.
findings.claim_source_sentence: Of the 42 symmetric (inhibitory) synapses formed by the reconstructed segment, 88% were with spiny dendrites of presumed granule cells, and 67% were with dendritic spines that also receive an asymmetric (excitatory) contact from an unlabeled axon terminal.
findings.evidence: Intracellular labelling, serial-section electron microscopy and postembedding GABA immunocytochemistry of hilar somatostatinergic interneuron axon arbors in rat dentate gyrus.
findings.effect_size: 88% of 42 symmetric synapses onto granule cell spiny dendrites; 67% onto spines also receiving excitatory contacts; 55% of molecular-layer GABAergic synapses with spines
findings.effect_size_source_sentence: Of the 42 symmetric (inhibitory) synapses formed by the reconstructed segment, 88% were with spiny dendrites of presumed granule cells, and 67% were with dendritic spines that also receive an asymmetric (excitatory) contact from an unlabeled axon terminal.
findings.study_system: Rat dentate gyrus hilar somatostatinergic interneurons, electron microscopy

findings.claim: In lithium-pilocarpine epileptic rats, somatostatin, NPY and parvalbumin interneurons are all reduced in the hilus of the sclerotic hippocampus with dendritic-targeting hilar interneurons most vulnerable, while surviving somatostatin fibres sprout into CA1.
findings.claim_source_sentence: Compared with age-matched control rats, there were fewer SS/NPY/PV-immunoreactive (IR) interneurons in the hilus of the sclerotic hippocampus in pilocarpine-treated rats; hilar dentritic inhibitory interneurons were most vulnerable.
findings.evidence: Immunohistochemistry for somatostatin, NPY and parvalbumin with cell counts and fibre analysis in the lithium-pilocarpine rat model of temporal lobe epilepsy.
findings.effect_size: Qualitative: fewer SS/NPY/PV interneurons in the sclerotic hilus; SS-immunoreactive sprouting in CA1
findings.study_system: Rat hippocampus after lithium-pilocarpine status epilepticus (sclerotic hippocampus)

findings.claim: Layer 5 motor cortex parvalbumin interneurons are hypoactive in late pre-symptomatic SOD1-G93A mice, and chemogenetically increasing their activity restores intracortical inhibition, reduces pyramidal hyperexcitability, delays motor deficit onset and extends survival — causal evidence that interneuron hypofunction drives cortical hyperexcitability in ALS.
findings.claim_source_sentence: We discovered that using adeno-associated virus-mediated delivery of chemogenetic technology targeted to increase the activity of the interneurons within layer 5 of the primary motor cortex, we were able to rescue intracortical inhibition and reduce pyramidal neuron hyperexcitability.
findings.evidence: Patch-clamp recordings from identified interneurons plus AAV-DREADD chemogenetic activation in layer 5 primary motor cortex of SOD1-G93A mice with behavioural and survival outcomes.
findings.effect_size: Qualitative: rescue of intracortical inhibition, delayed onset, slowed progression and increased lifespan; no numeric effect size in abstract
findings.study_system: SOD1-G93A transgenic mouse primary motor cortex layer 5 parvalbumin interneurons

findings.claim: TDP-43 Q331K knock-in mice show reduced parvalbumin interneuron numbers already at postnatal day 14, and human post-mortem prefrontal cortex from sporadic and C9orf72 ALS shows the same parvalbumin interneuron paucity, suggesting a developmental component to interneuron loss in TDP-43 proteinopathy.
findings.claim_source_sentence: Finally, analysis of human post-mortem prefrontal cortices confirmed a paucity of PV+ interneurons in the prefrontal cortex in cases with both sporadic ALS and ALS linked to C9orf72 mutations.
findings.evidence: Structural MRI-guided post-mortem histology in TDP-43 Q331K knock-in mice at juvenile and adult ages, with parallel human post-mortem prefrontal cortex immunohistochemistry.
findings.effect_size: Reduced PV+ interneuron numbers in mutant mice from P14 and in human sporadic and C9orf72 ALS prefrontal cortex (direction only; no numeric value in abstract)
findings.study_system: TDP-43 Q331K knock-in mice and human post-mortem ALS prefrontal cortex

findings.claim: In prenatal SOD1 mouse spinal cord, depolarising GABAergic/glycinergic synaptic events fail to inhibit motoneurons with low input resistance — the population that becomes vulnerable — indicating that inhibitory synaptic control of motor neurons is already compromised embryonically in ALS.
findings.claim_source_sentence: We found that GABAergic/glycinergic synaptic events do not properly inhibit ALS MNs with low input resistance, most probably corresponding to future vulnerable MNs.
findings.evidence: Patch-clamp recordings of depolarising GABA/glycine postsynaptic potentials in embryonic SOD1 mouse spinal motoneurons combined with compartmental modelling.
findings.effect_size: Qualitative: loss of inhibitory efficacy restricted to low input resistance motoneurons; no numeric effect size in abstract
findings.study_system: Embryonic SOD1 mouse spinal motoneurons, patch-clamp and computational model

findings.claim: Short-interval intracortical inhibition in ALS is phenotype-dependent: bulbar-onset patients show reduced inhibition at all interstimulus intervals whereas patients with a pyramidal phenotype have normal SICI, so GABAergic interneuron dysfunction is not uniform across ALS phenotypes.
findings.claim_source_sentence: Compared with healthy controls, Bulbar patients had significantly less inhibition at all ISIs, while SICI in Pyramidal patients was normal, and in Classic patients intermediate.
findings.evidence: Threshold-tracking paired-pulse TMS measuring SICI and SICF across ALS clinical phenotypes versus healthy controls.
findings.effect_size: Pyramidal n = 12, Classic n = 20, bulbar group separately analysed; bulbar reduced SICI at all ISIs, pyramidal normal

findings.study_system: Human ALS patients stratified by clinical phenotype, threshold-tracking TMS

findings.claim: In multiple sclerosis primary motor cortex, parvalbumin interneurons are selectively reduced in layer 2 while calretinin interneuron numbers are unchanged, showing subtype-selective interneuron loss in MS cortical grey matter.
findings.claim_source_sentence: Our results indicate a significant reduction in the number of PV interneurons within layer 2 of the multiple sclerosis primary motor cortex with no concurrent change in number of calretinin positive neurons.
findings.evidence: Quantitative immunohistochemistry for parvalbumin and calretinin across cortical layers of post-mortem MS and control primary motor cortex.
findings.effect_size: Significant reduction of layer 2 PV interneurons; no change in calretinin neurons (no numeric value in abstract)
findings.study_system: Human post-mortem multiple sclerosis primary motor cortex

findings.claim: CSF somatostatin and NPY, the two peptides marking cortical SST interneurons, are correlated with each other in frontotemporal dementia but not in Alzheimer's disease, and somatostatin level tracks dementia severity in AD, indicating disease-specific SST interneuron peptide signatures.
findings.claim_source_sentence: The CSF levels of the two neuropeptides somatostatin and NPY were significantly correlated in FTD (p < 0.02), but not in AD.
findings.evidence: CSF somatostatin-like and NPY-like immunoreactivity measured in FTD and AD patients and correlated with 54 clinical items.
findings.effect_size: Somatostatin–NPY correlation significant in FTD (p < 0.02) but not AD; somatostatin negatively correlated with dementia severity in AD (p < 0.013)
findings.effect_size_source_sentence: The CSF levels of the two neuropeptides somatostatin and NPY were significantly correlated in FTD (p < 0.02), but not in AD.
findings.study_system: Human patients with frontotemporal dementia (n = 22) and Alzheimer's disease (n = 34), cerebrospinal fluid neuropeptides

findings.claim: GABAergic interneurons and medial ganglionic eminence organoids derived from Down syndrome iPSCs show perinuclear mitochondrial clustering and impaired oxidative phosphorylation that is corrected by blocking the DSCAM-PAK1 pathway, giving a trisomy-21 gene-dosage mechanism for interneuron dysfunction.
findings.claim_source_sentence: The mitochondria were abnormally clustered in the perinuclear region of GABA neurons and cell in MGE organoids from DS patients, which exhibited impaired mitochondrial function as assessed by seahorse oxidative phosphorylation assay.
findings.evidence: Down syndrome patient and control iPSC-derived GABAergic interneurons and MGE organoids with mitochondrial imaging, Seahorse respirometry and DSCAM-PAK1 pathway manipulation.
findings.effect_size: Impaired oxidative phosphorylation in DS GABAergic neurons, corrected by DSCAM-PAK1 inhibition (direction only; no numeric value in abstract)
findings.study_system: Down syndrome patient-derived iPSC GABAergic interneurons and MGE organoids

findings.claim: Synthesis of evidence across Alzheimer's disease, frontotemporal dementia and dementia with Lewy bodies argues that parvalbumin interneuron dysfunction is the shared substrate of cortical hyperexcitability and gamma rhythm disruption in these dementias.
findings.claim_source_sentence: However, no attempt has been made to integrate these findings into a coherent pathophysiological framework addressing the contribution of PV+ interneuron dysfunction to the generation of cortical hyperexcitability and gamma rhythm disruption in FTD and DLB.
findings.evidence: Narrative synthesis of experimental and clinical studies of PV interneuron impairment, cortical hyperexcitability and gamma oscillations in AD, FTD and DLB.
findings.effect_size: Qualitative synthesis; no primary effect size (review)
findings.study_system: Review of human and animal studies in Alzheimer's disease, frontotemporal dementia and dementia with Lewy bodies

findings.claim: Ts65Dn Down syndrome mice develop an age-dependent increase in GABAergic innervation of dentate granule cells driven by a greater number of basket cells, and normalising App copy number restores basket cell number, implicating APP dosage in inhibitory over-innervation.
findings.claim_source_sentence: Then we aimed to identify the gene/s whose overexpression could be linked to increased number of BCs in Ts65Dn and found that deleting the third copy of App gene in Ts65Dn mice led to normalization of the number of BCs in these mice.
findings.evidence: Morphometric analysis of GABAergic terminals and basket cell counts in dentate gyrus of young and old Ts65Dn mice, 2N controls and Ts65Dn with App copy normalised.
findings.effect_size: Significant increase in basket cell number in Ts65Dn versus controls, normalised by deleting the third App copy (no numeric value in abstract)
findings.study_system: Ts65Dn mouse model of Down syndrome, dentate gyrus GABAergic interneurons

findings.claim: In Ts65Dn hippocampus the numbers of calbindin, calretinin, NPY and VIP interneurons are increased in CA1 and CA3 while parvalbumin cell numbers are unaffected, showing that inhibitory excess in Down syndrome is subtype-restricted.
findings.claim_source_sentence: In agreement with this observation, we have observed an increase in the number of inhibitory neurons in CA1 and CA3, mainly interneurons expressing calbindin, calretinin, NPY and VIP, whereas parvalbumin cell numbers were not affected.
findings.evidence: Immunohistochemical quantification of synaptic markers and inhibitory neuron subtypes across hippocampal subfields in Ts65Dn mice and euploid controls.
findings.effect_size: Increase in calbindin, calretinin, NPY and VIP interneurons in CA1/CA3; parvalbumin unchanged (no numeric value in abstract)
findings.study_system: Ts65Dn mouse hippocampus, interneuron subtype immunohistochemistry

findings.claim: Translating-ribosome profiling of neuronal subtypes in pre-symptomatic fatal familial insomnia and CJD mouse models shows that somatostatin neurons have the most prominent gene expression changes of any neuronal subtype, with shared GABAergic responses across the two prion diseases while glutamatergic responses are disease-specific.
findings.claim_source_sentence: GSEA demonstrated similar enrichment patterns of functional terms for GABAergic cell types in both FFI and CJD, whereas responses in glutamatergic neurons were disease specific.
findings.evidence: Cell-type-specific translational (RiboTag) profiling of SST, PV and glutamatergic neurons in pre-symptomatic mouse models of fatal familial insomnia and Creutzfeldt-Jakob disease, with weighted gene co-expression network analysis.
findings.effect_size: SST+ neurons showed the most prominent gene expression changes of the profiled subtypes, most marked in FFI; three hub genes including Depdc5 and Mta3 differentially expressed in FFI SST neurons
findings.effect_size_source_sentence: We found SST<sup>+</sup> neurons showed the most prominent gene expression changes in both diseases, especially in FFI, with high similari
findings.study_system: Pre-symptomatic mouse models of fatal familial insomnia and Creutzfeldt-Jakob disease, neuronal subtype translational profiling (preprint)

findings.claim: In a genetic (Pten knockout) model of epilepsy-associated hippocampal pathology, somatostatin interneuron density falls by roughly 13-22% across subregions, yet the surviving cells show no increase in oxidative-stress or apoptosis markers, retain their SST molecular phenotype, and maintain axonal output density — so reduced SST counts need not indicate ongoing interneuron death or loss of inhibitory output.
findings.claim_source_sentence: However, there was no difference in the proportion of 3-NT+, eGFP-SST cells in the dentate hilus between DGC-Pten KOs and controls (Figure 3B; Control, 38.47% ± 2.08% of eGFP+ cells were 3-NT+; KO, 38.61% ± 2.62%; p = 0.9684), and no colocalization of eGFP and cleaved caspase-3 was observed (Figure 3C; Control, 0.0% ± 0.0% of eGFP+ cells were cleaved caspase-3+; KO, 0.0% ± 0.0%).
findings.evidence: Fate-mapping of SST interneurons with quadruple transgenic labelling, density measurements across hippocampal subregions, 3-nitrotyrosine and cleaved caspase-3 labelling, and molecular-layer axon density analysis in DGC-Pten knockout mice.
findings.effect_size: Hilar SST density 4,395 ± 182 vs 3,411 ± 322 cells/mm3 (p = 0.0334); 3-NT+ proportion 38.47% vs 38.61% (p = 0.9684); SST immunoreactivity 84.17% vs 84.76% of eGFP+ cells (p = 0.8212)
findings.effect_size_source_sentence: Similarly, the majority of eGFP+ neurons were immunoreactive for SST, again with no difference between groups (Figure 4C; Control, 84.17% ± 2.07%; KO, 84.76% ± 1.54%; p = 0.8212).
findings.study_system: Dentate granule cell Pten knockout mice with fate-mapped eGFP-SST interneurons (epilepsy model)

findings.claim: After controlled cortical impact, surviving hilar inhibitory interneurons receive de novo excitatory input from dentate granule cells and CA3 pyramidal cells and become hyperactive, a reorganisation that is only partly mTOR-dependent and may partially compensate for interneuron loss rather than simply reflecting it.
findings.claim_source_sentence: Synaptic reorganization originating from DGCs and CA3 pyramidal cells onto surviving hilar interneurons may partially compensate for the loss of these cells after brain injury.
findings.evidence: Glutamate uncaging circuit mapping and whole-cell recordings from eGFP-labelled hilar interneurons 8-12 weeks after controlled cortical impact, with and without chronic rapamycin.
findings.effect_size: 43.33 ± 11.97% positive responding sites after CA3 photostimulation in injured mice versus controls (Dunn's p = 0.0033)
findings.effect_size_source_sentence: Interneurons from CCI-injured, vehicle-treated mice exhibited a significantly increased percentage of positive responding sites after CA3 pyramidal cell photostimulation relative to controls (CCI ipsi = 43.33 ± 11.97%; Dunn’s: vs control p = 0.0033; Fig.
findings.study_system: Mouse dentate hilus after controlled cortical impact traumatic brain injury (GIN eGFP interneurons)

findings.claim: In kindling and electrically induced status epilepticus, somatostatin and NPY immunoreactivity and mRNA are markedly increased in hilar interneurons at seizure stages that precede or accompany epileptogenesis, the opposite direction to the peptide loss reported in chronic epileptic tissue.
findings.claim_source_sentence: At the preconvulsive stage 2 of kindling and after three consecutive tonic-clonic seizures (stage 5) but not after a single-discharge (AD), somatostatin and NPY immunoreactivity (IR) were markedly increased in interneurons of the deep hilus and the polymorphic cell layer and their presumed projections to the outer molecular layer of the dentate gyrus.
findings.evidence: Immunocytochemistry and in situ hybridisation for somatostatin and NPY across kindling stages and after electrically induced status epilepticus in rat hippocampus.
findings.effect_size: Marked increase in somatostatin and NPY immunoreactivity and mRNA in deep hilar and polymorphic layer interneurons at kindling stage 2 and after three tonic-clonic seizures (direction only; no numeric value in abstract)
findings.study_system: Rat hippocampus, kindling and electrically induced status epilepticus models

findings.claim: CSF somatostatin in demented patients rose significantly over three months of an activating psychosocial care programme, in parallel with improved intellectual and motor function, showing that somatostatin measures in dementia are state-dependent and reversible rather than a fixed index of interneuron degeneration.
findings.claim_source_sentence: Concomitantly, the SRIF concentrations in CSF were significantly elevated in the experimental group and not affected in the control group.
findings.evidence: Controlled three-month nursing-home intervention study with dementia rating scales, psychological testing and lumbar puncture neuropeptide measurement before and after.
findings.effect_size: Significant elevation of CSF somatostatin in the intervention group with no change in the control group
findings.effect_size_source_sentence: Concomitantly, the SRIF concentrations in CSF were significantly elevated in the experimental group and not affected in the control group.
findings.study_system: Elderly demented nursing-home patients, intervention (n = 17) versus usual care (n = 18), CSF neuropeptides

findings.claim: A single-nucleus atlas of human antero-median thalamus across GRN-associated and sporadic TDP-43 frontotemporal dementia finds two inhibitory neuronal populations markedly depleted with impaired GABAergic communication, while specific excitatory populations are comparatively resilient — placing inhibitory vulnerability outside the cortex in FTD.
findings.claim_source_sentence: In particular, two inhibitory neuronal populations were markedly depleted in FTD, which was accompanied by impaired GABAergic communication.
findings.evidence: Integrated single-nucleus RNA sequencing atlas of 331,065 nuclei from 92 individuals spanning GRN-FTD, sporadic FTD-TDP, Alzheimer's disease and controls.
findings.effect_size: 331,065 nuclei from 92 individuals across three cohorts; two inhibitory populations markedly depleted
findings.study_system: Human post-mortem antero-median thalamus, GRN and sporadic TDP-43 frontotemporal dementia, Alzheimer's disease and controls (preprint)

arg_01.thesis: Cortical disinhibition in ALS: robust at the group level, heterogeneous within cohorts - Establish reduced GABA-A-mediated short-interval intracortical inhibition as the most consistent inhibitory finding in ALS, then set the pooled meta-analytic effect against the single-cohort distribution in which only half of patients are hyperexcitable and a quarter are cortically inexcitable, and note the GABA-B long-interval null and the absence of the deficit in asymptomatic mutation carriers.
arg_01.synthesis: Subsection 1 of 6. Anchored on 1 pre-extracted cross-study comparison(s); 4 findings in this package carry the anchored metrics directly. Remaining support for this subsection is drawn from arg_unanchored.

arg_02.thesis: Which interneurons? PV depletion is measured, SST is inferred - Assemble the PV density literature across TDP-43 proteinopathy, demyelination, trauma and epilepsy - clustering around 25-50% - and show that the one human hippocampal study with pTau staging finds no change. Then state the asymmetry plainly: the SST evidence in these conditions is depletion magnitudes from epileptogenic, traumatic and tauopathy insults in rodents, plus tau-bearing dystrophic SST survivors, with no human ALS/FTLD SST quantification retrieved.
arg_02.synthesis: Subsection 2 of 6. Anchored on 2 pre-extracted cross-study comparison(s); 11 findings in this package carry the anchored metrics directly. Remaining support for this subsection is drawn from arg_unanchored.

arg_03.thesis: The SST-driven disinhibition model and its single source - Present the TDP-43 model in which hyperactive SST interneurons suppress PV cells and disinhibit layer 5 pyramidal neurons, against the wobbler model in which hyperexcitability follows globally reduced inhibition with decreased SST and PV density. subsections.title: Cortical disinhibition in ALS: robust at the group level, heterogeneous within cohorts
subsections.job: Establish reduced GABA-A-mediated short-interval intracortical inhibition as the most consistent inhibitory finding in ALS, then set the pooled meta-analytic effect against the single-cohort distribution in which only half of patients are hyperexcitable and a quarter are cortically inexcitable, and note the GABA-B long-interval null and the absence of the deficit in asymptomatic mutation carriers.

subsections.title: Which interneurons? PV depletion is measured, SST is inferred
subsections.job: Assemble the PV density literature across TDP-43 proteinopathy, demyelination, trauma and epilepsy - clustering around 25-50% - and show that the one human hippocampal study with pTau staging finds no change. Then state the asymmetry plainly: the SST evidence in these conditions is depletion magnitudes from epileptogenic, traumatic and tauopathy insults in rodents, plus tau-bearing dystrophic SST survivors, with no human ALS/FTLD SST quantification retrieved.

subsections.title: The SST-driven disinhibition model and its single source
subsections.job: Present the TDP-43 model in which hyperactive SST interneurons suppress PV cells and disinhibit layer 5 pyramidal neurons, against the wobbler model in which hyperexcitability follows globally reduced inhibition with decreased SST and PV density. Name this as the clearest instance in the review of a mechanistic account carried by one unreplicated study.

subsections.title: Prion disease, Down syndrome and traumatic injury: loss of cells or loss of markers and nets
subsections.job: Use these literatures as a controlled comparison of the marker problem: early PV neuron loss in human CJD against perineuronal-net loss with intact PV counts in ME7; aggregate load under-represented in GABAergic neurons; 71% PV loss in contusion against fully preserved counts with 46-67% loss of perisomatic terminals after undercut; anatomically increased PV basket cells against functionally reduced perisomatic inhibition in Ts65Dn.

subsections.title: Multiple sclerosis: four modalities, four answers
subsections.job: Show that the direction of the inhibitory deficit in MS depends on the level measured - reduced bulk GABA by spectroscopy, increased GABA-A receptor binding by flumazenil PET, altered CSF parvalbumin - and that receptor upregulation compensating for reduced transmitter is as consistent with the data as a graded inhibitory failure.

subsections.title: Scope discipline: what belongs in an SST review
subsections.job: State explicitly which of these conditions have SST-level evidence and which are included only as controlled comparisons for the marker problem, so the breadth of the section is not mistaken for breadth of SST evidence.

evidence_gaps_to_state.topic: Somatostatin interneurons in human ALS and FTLD motor/frontal cortex
evidence_gaps_to_state.what_is_missing: Direct quantification of SST interneuron density, morphology or transcriptional state in post-mortem human ALS or FTLD cortex. Database searching returned only 10 records for somatostatin combined with amyotrophic lateral sclerosis in title/abstract, and the human cortical quantifications retrieved in this cluster measure parvalbumin, not somatostatin.
evidence_gaps_to_state.why_it_matters: The mechanistic model of SST-driven disinhibition rests on a single mouse TDP-43 study; without human SST data the translation from mouse circuit physiology to human cortical hyperexcitability is unsupported.

evidence_gaps_to_state.topic: Interneuron pathology in chronic traumatic encephalopathy
evidence_gaps_to_state.what_is_missing: Any quantitative interneuron study in human CTE. Title/abstract searches for chronic traumatic encephalopathy combined with somatostatin, parvalbumin or interneuron returned zero records in Europe PMC.
evidence_gaps_to_state.why_it_matters: CTE is grouped with other tauopathies in reviews of interneuron vulnerability, but the inhibitory-circuit evidence attributed to it comes entirely from experimental TBI models, not from CTE tissue.

evidence_gaps_to_state.topic: Causal direction of cortical hyperexcitability in ALS
evidence_gaps_to_state.what_is_missing: Primary experimental demonstration in human tissue that interneuron loss causes, rather than follows, cortical hyperexcitability. Human evidence retrieved here is indirect (paired-pulse TMS-EEG inhibition measures) or post-mortem cross-sectional (PV density).
evidence_gaps_to_state.why_it_matters: Risk of false consensus: the interneuron-loss explanation for ALS cortical hyperexcitability is widely stated, yet the causal experiments exist only in rodent models and the one multi-model synaptic study finds no presymptomatic E:I change.

evidence_gaps_to_state.topic: Whether parvalbumin loss reflects cell death or loss of marker expression
evidence_gaps_to_state.what_is_missing: Studies combining a PV-independent interneuron marker (e.g., genetic lineage label or pan-interneuron nuclear marker) with PV immunoreactivity in the same degenerating tissue.
evidence_gaps_to_state.why_it_matters: Most reported PV deficits across these diseases are immunoreactivity-based; if PV expression is activity-dependent and downregulated rather than the cells being lost, the therapeutic implication inverts from replacement to reactivation.

evidence_gaps_to_state.topic: Universality of cortical hyperexcitability in ALS
evidence_gaps_to_state.what_is_missing: Primary data reconciling group-level meta-analytic SICI reduction with the finding that a quarter of ALS patients are cortically inexcitable and a quarter normal; no longitudinal within-patient study tracking transition between excitability phenotypes.
evidence_gaps_to_state.why_it_matters: Risk of false consensus: 'cortical hyperexcitability is a hallmark of ALS' is repeated across reviews but the within-cohort distribution shows it applies to about half of patients.

evidence_gaps_to_state.topic: Somatostatin interneurons specifically (as opposed to parvalbumin) in prion disease, MS and CTE
evidence_gaps_to_state.what_is_missing: Direct quantification of SST interneuron density or function in human prion disease, MS cortical lesions and chronic traumatic encephalopathy; available human work is dominated by parvalbumin and perineuronal net markers, with SST evidence limited to rodent translational profiling.
evidence_gaps_to_state.why_it_matters: Section claims about SST interneuron vulnerability in these conditions would rest on extrapolation from PV data and from rodent models rather than direct human SST measurements.

evidence_gaps_to_state.topic: Interneuron marker loss versus cell death
evidence_gaps_to_state.what_is_missing: Studies combining an interneuron-subtype marker with a marker-independent cell identity readout (genetic labelling, in situ transcript, stereology of total neurons) in the same tissue for FTLD, prion disease and trauma.
evidence_gaps_to_state.why_it_matters: Several conflicts in this cluster (prion PV loss, post-traumatic PV loss) may be artefacts of marker downregulation rather than interneuron death, which changes whether therapy should target survival or function.

certified_evidence_limits.search_coverage: Europe PMC-dominant retrieval. Endpoints actually used: Europe PMC REST search (resultType=core) and fullTextXML, NCBI E-utilities efetch (db=pmc), CrossRef. No other database contributed a comparable share, so coverage claims must be scoped to these sources.
certified_evidence_limits.citation_chasing: None. No backward or forward citation chasing was performed. No section may claim completeness of coverage; write 'no study examining X was retrieved by these searches', never 'no study has examined X'.
certified_evidence_limits.fulltext_shortfall_concentration: The shortfall is concentrated in pre-2000 closed-access postmortem and CSF literature (radioimmunoassay series), which is recorded at abstract level only. Each conflict carries a primary axis and the full set of axes present, since most of these disagreements are genuinely multi-axis. suggested_paragraph_groupings.what_explains_the_discrepancy: Direction of somatostatin interneuron change underlying cortical hyperexcitability. The TDP-43 model attributes layer 5 pyramidal hyperexcitability to hyperactive SST interneurons that disinhibit the network via suppression of PV cells, whereas the wobbler model attributes hyperexcitability to globally reduced GABAergic inhibition with decreased density of both SST and PV interneurons. Dimension of disagreement: whether SST interneurons are functionally gained or lost, and whether disinhibition is circuit-level (SST-to-PV) or arises from overall interneuron depletion.

Group-level meta-analysis presents reduced intracortical inhibition as a near-universal ALS signature, whereas phenotyping of a large single cohort finds hyperexcitability in only half of patients and frank cortical inexcitability in a quarter. The conflict is between the pooled mean effect and the within-cohort distribution, bearing on whether GABAergic interneuron failure is a universal or a subgroup phenomenon.

Whether reduced somatostatin interneuron counts after an epileptogenic insult reflect cell death. Counting studies interpret the missing SST-immunoreactive cells as selective interneuron death, whereas genetic fate-mapping of the same population finds reduced density with no increase in oxidative-stress or apoptosis markers, unchanged SST phenotype among labelled cells, and preserved axonal output — implicating marker/phenotype change and sampling rather than loss of inhibitory output.

Whether GABAergic interneurons are selectively vulnerable or relatively resistant in prion disease. The histopathological study reports severe and early selective loss of cortical parvalbumin-positive GABAergic neurons in scrapie and CJD, while the prion-propagation study finds PrP-Sc aggregates under-represented in GABA-positive neurons and concentrated in excitatory neurons. Dimension of disagreement: whether aggregate load predicts degeneration, and whether PV+ loss reflects cell death versus loss of the parvalbumin marker.

Whether prion disease causes actual loss of parvalbumin interneurons or only degradation of their perineuronal extracellular matrix: human CJD tissue reports early PV neuron loss, while the ME7 mouse model shows perineuronal net loss with intact PV interneuron numbers through 20 weeks post-inoculation. The disagreement may reflect species/model, disease stage, or the confound that PV immunoreactivity falls before cell death.
